question.question: A Docker image built with a multi-stage build where the final stage uses a distroless base image will have a smaller attack surface than the same image built with a single-stage build using a full Ubuntu base, assuming identical application code and dependencies.
question.explanation: Multi-stage builds allow copying only necessary artifacts (compiled binaries, installed packages, model weights) to a minimal final stage. Distroless images contain only the application and its runtime dependencies—no shell, package manager, or standard Linux utilities—significantly reducing the attack surface compared to a full Ubuntu base that includes hundreds of unnecessary binaries and libraries.
